claim: EU leaders meeting in Brussels on Thursday 26 November 2026 politically agree that Pablo Hernández de Cos should be the next President of the European Central Bank.

runs.reason:
**Base rate.** The closest precedent gives a rough starting point of one success in two summit opportunities, not a reliable historical rate. In 2019, EU leaders deferred their top-jobs talks at the June 20–21 summit, then publicly backed Christine Lagarde on July 2, the final day of the next summit, before the formal appointment. That shows both that political backing can be announced separately and that the timing can slip. ([consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/meetings/european-council/2019/06/20-21/))

**What moves this case.** **Up:** On November 12, EFE reported that leaders were aiming for a political agreement at the November 26 Euro Summit specifically. On November 20, *El País* reported that France and Germany had put forward candidates for the other two ECB vacancies and that sources familiar with the talks favored Hernández de Cos for president. **Up, with a caveat:** Costa’s November 24 invitation confirms that leaders will address ECB succession and that the Euro Summit starts Thursday at 10:00, but it does not promise a Thursday decision. **Down:** *El País* still listed Klaas Knot as a candidate on November 22. A November 23 Caja Ingenieros note referred to his withdrawal, but I found no official confirmation, so I give that report limited weight. ([efe.com](https://efe.com/economia/2026-11-12/candidatos-presidencia-bce/))

**Window risk.** I put the chance that the Thursday Euro Summit itself is canceled or moved at roughly 2%. The bigger risk is that the summit goes ahead but leaders leave the ECB item unresolved on Thursday, or hold the announcement until Friday. I’m more confident that Hernández de Cos is the eventual choice than that a qualifying endorsement is public by Thursday at 23:59 Brussels time. ([consilium.europa.eu](https://www.consilium.europa.eu/en/press/press-releases/2026/11/20/weekly-schedule-of-president-antonio-costa/?utm_source=openai))

mber Special European Council, President António Costa confirmed that leaders "will also take the time to address the renewal of the European Central Bank leadership, with a view to a timely decision," and placed the Euro Summit as the first session of the meeting starting at 10:00 Brussels time on Thursday 26 November, prior to breaking into bilateral negotiations on the Multiannual Financial Framework (MFF).

### 3. Strongest Reason the Obvious Outcome Might Fail
Even with the Franco-German-Spanish package in place and the Euro Summit scheduled for 10:00 on Thursday 26 November, the primary focus of the two-day Special European Council is a highly contentious negotiation over the 2028–2034 Multiannual Financial Framework (which France and several other states have sharply criticized) and 2027 Ukraine financing. There is a meaningful risk that leaders either hold back the announcement of the ECB leadership deal until the full summit concludes on Friday 27 November (which would resolve the claim NO due to the strict 23:59 Thursday deadline), or that backers of Klaas Knot or critics of the Governing Council's gender imbalance delay consensus or insist that the Eurogroup/ECOFIN formally process the package first. However, because the Euro Summit takes place on Thursday morning and the criterion allows confirmation via at least two major wire agencies citing officials or leaders, a Thursday agreement on Hernández de Cos is highly likely to be reported before midnight.

runs.reason:
The political package is largely locked, but the claim turns on a same-day publicity rule that the summit timetable does not guarantee.

Comparable ECB successions are usually settled once France and Germany align and the qualified-majority arithmetic is in hand; late reversals after that point are uncommon. What is less common is a criterion that fails if the same deal is only made public on the second day of a two-day summit. Here the substance points to Pablo Hernández de Cos, while the clock points to a material miss risk.

Costa’s invitation letter of 24 November puts “the renewal of the European Central Bank leadership, with a view to a timely decision” on the 26–27 November special European Council, which opens at 10:00 on Thursday with a Euro Summit. That follows an explicit October plan to choose a candidate in November so a December appointment is still possible before Christine Lagarde leaves on 7 February 2027. The package itself is already public: on 17 November Germany backed de Cos and claimed the chief-economist seat for Markus Brunnermeier; the Financial Times reported that Emmanuel Macron had told Friedrich Merz in Dublin he would support de Cos if France dropped its claim to that post. On 20 November France and Germany filed Laurence Boone and Brunnermeier, which Reuters and Politico described as completing the deal that puts de Cos on track for the presidency. El País reported on 22 November that Klaas Knot is already treated as the loser and that only de Cos had been received by Macron.

Those facts pull this case above a generic “will leaders agree sometime” base rate. They do not remove the Thursday cutoff. Knot had not clearly withdrawn as of 20–21 November, so a clean sole-candidate recommendation was still blocked and a visible vote remained possible. The Euro Summit slot described by Costa is an economic briefing and a farewell to Lagarde, not an explicit decision point, and he plans to share conclusions on Friday. A pre-cooked personnel item can be nodded through on Thursday and briefed the same evening — wires cite officials within hours when that happens — but it can just as easily be parked until the Friday press moment, or pushed to the 17–18 December European Council if the budget fight consumes the room. Either of those is a NO under the criterion as written, even if de Cos is the person everyone expects.
